items.title: easyJet’s efficient refuelling and EU packaging rules: The sustainability success stories of the week
items.summary: As part of our Mission Possible campaign, edie delivers this member-exclusive weekly round-up of five of the best sustainable business success stories of the week.

items.title: Government unveils £65m package for farmers as drought pressures mount
items.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has announced a £65m funding package for English farming to help the industry manage drought impacts and protect yields.

items.title: Government launches consultation on ZEV mandate targets and flexibilities
items.summary: The Government has launched a two-month consultation on whether targets for zero-emission vehicle sales in the UK should be weakened.

items.title: Heatwave spiked EU solar output 17%, research finds
items.summary: Research from energy think tank Ember has found solar output in Europe rose 17% during the heatwaves in June and July 2026.

items.title: Q&A: What does China’s 15th five-year plan for coal mean for climate action?
items.summary: China has published a new five-year plan for coal, the latest in a slew of important policy documents for the country’s energy transition.

items.title: Sustainability Uncovered episode 47: SAFs, festivals and a sustainable summer
items.summary: The latest episode of edie’s long-standing Sustainability Uncovered podcast is now live.

items.summary: Event Date: 20/10/2026 | 1:00 pm UK | 8:00 am US East Coast ET | 5:00 am US West Coast PT | 2:00 pm Central Europe CET/CEST Join our 45-minute masterclass on 15 September 2026 to understand how the UK CBAM will shape your sustainability strategies.

items.title: Europe’s hydrogen projects stuck in feasibility stage
items.summary: According to the Energy Industries Council (EIC), Europe’s hydrogen market is faltering due to lower demand and projects being stuck in the feasibility stage.

items.title: Can Britain deliver net-zero without talking about climate?
items.summary: As politicians increasingly frame climate action through housing, health, jobs, energy security and economic growth, the UK may be entering a new era of climate politics – one that risks pushing climate back down the agenda.
